findings.claim: The new parenthesis-depth scan requires the reason's parentheses to be balanced. A reason with an unbalanced parenthesis (for example "3 (works :) fine)" or "3 (see foo( )") was accepted before and is now refused as a malformed trailer. The failure is closed and visible, and it follows the commit's stated intent. It is still a change in which reasons are accepted, and the tests do not cover it (only the extra-close case is tested).
The blank-reason check only strips one trailing ")" before trimming. A reason such as "3 (())" or "3 (( ))" has no real text but still passes, so the blank-reason rule is incomplete.

evidence: Traced "none (x) 3 (y)": the first ")" brings depth to 0 before the last byte, so the value is returned unchanged and ParseRisk refuses it. This is the intended fix.
Traced "2 (x), 3 (y)": same path, refused as intended.
Traced "3 (a (b))": depth returns to 0 only at the last byte, so the head "3" is returned. Nested reasons still work.
Traced "3 ( )": the blank check returns the value unchanged, so it is refused.
